note: The simplest string mutation there is: an ASCII character into an ASCII string. Emacs answers (122 "zbc") -- `aset` returns the character it stored and the string is changed in place. kg refuses by name, `unsupported: aset on a string`, because a fe string is a chain of seven-byte cells whose shape a byte write has to preserve. fe's own `primitive-aset-string` row records the same refusal from the fe side; this is the kg-side complement, and it is the one Phase 25.1 makes work.
